test_title: PYST 52: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 08 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following sectors contributed the most to India’s defence exports in FY 2023-24?

options.text: The private sector contributed about 60% and DPSUs about 40%
The private sector and DPSUs equally

solution:
The correct answer is __**The private sector contributed about 60% and DPSUs about 40%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The private sector played a significant role in India's defence exports during FY 2023-24, contributing about 60% of the total exports.
 
• Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) contributed around 40%, showcasing their importance in the defence manufacturing ecosystem.
 
• The increase in private sector contribution is attributed to the government's initiatives to promote private participation in defence production, including the Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP) 2020.
 
• The government has incentivized private companies through policies like the simplification of the Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) and the establishment of defence industrial corridors.
 
• India's defence exports in FY 2023-24 surpassed Rs. 15,000 crore, indicating a significant leap in global competitiveness and self-reliance in defence manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Technological Advancements:**

 
 
• Missile Systems: Advanced indigenous missiles like Akash (SAM), BrahMos (supersonic cruise), and development of hypersonic weapons.
 
• Air Defense: Multi-layered systems (Sudarshan Chakra/S-400, Akash, Barak-8, BMD program) to counter various aerial threats, including drones.
 
• Naval Power: Indigenous carriers, advanced destroyers, and nuclear submarines enhance "blue-water" capabilities.
 
• Emerging Tech: Investing in Directed Energy Weapons (lasers, microwaves) and cyber/electronic warfare.
